steps.title: Running the Whole Plan Yourself
steps.lede: With the plan, retrieval, cleaning, modeling, statistics, and visualization steps all defined, what is left is carrying the whole thing out yourself — end to end — without being walked through each step again.

blocks.text: During the design phase, the commission is converted into an analytical plan, with some iteration expected as the solution is developed. For the capstone, the workflow outline from earlier becomes that analytical plan, and it is normal to adjust it once the SQL, spreadsheet, and pandas work actually starts.

During the analysis phase, the planned analysis is carried out while progress and relevance are monitored, and appropriate records of the analysis conducted, changes, decisions, and assumptions made are maintained. As the capstone's query, cleaning, modeling, statistics, and figures get built, a decision log captures what changed and why.

nodes.label: Design phase
nodes.detail: Convert commission → analytical plan; iteration expected

nodes.label: Analysis phase
nodes.detail: Execute plan; monitor progress and relevance

nodes.label: Decision log
nodes.detail: Records of changes, decisions, and assumptions

blocks.alt_text: Two-phase flow: Design phase produces an analytical plan (with an iteration arrow back to Design), then Analysis phase produces both a decision log and the analytical outputs.

steps.title: What Belongs in the Decision Log?
steps.lede: During the analysis phase of the QuickShip capstone, which of the following should be recorded in the decision log?

public.prompt: During the analysis phase of the QuickShip capstone, you discover that one delivery zone has far fewer orders than expected. What should you do?

options.text: Record the discovery in your decision log, note how you handled it, and continue — monitoring whether it affects the analysis's relevance to the original question.
Ignore it and proceed — minor data issues do not affect the overall conclusion.
Restart the analysis from scratch — the plan is no longer valid.
Report the issue to the operations team immediately and wait for their instructions before continuing.

opt_record_monitor.message: Correct. During the analysis phase, appropriate records of the analysis conducted, changes, decisions, and assumptions made are maintained, while progress and relevance are monitored. Recording the discovery and how you handled it is exactly what the decision log is for.

opt_ignore.message: Ignoring a data issue without recording it violates the requirement to maintain appropriate records of changes and decisions. Even minor issues should be logged so the analysis remains transparent.

opt_restart.message: Restarting from scratch is not necessary for every data issue. The analysis phase involves monitoring progress and relevance and recording decisions — not abandoning the plan at the first complication.

opt_report_only.message: Stopping to wait for instructions is not always necessary. The analysis phase involves carrying out the planned analysis while monitoring and recording decisions. Record the issue and continue, flagging it in the decision log for the stakeholder's awareness.

correct.message: Right. The analysis phase requires maintaining records of changes, decisions, and assumptions while monitoring whether the analysis still answers the original question. That is what the decision log is for.

incorrect.message: During the analysis phase, you carry out the planned analysis while monitoring progress and relevance, and maintaining records of changes, decisions, and assumptions. Record the issue and continue.

hints: What is the purpose of a decision log during the analysis phase?
The analysis phase involves monitoring and recording — not ignoring issues or restarting.

steps.title: Execute the Capstone Plan
steps.lede: Using the QuickShip orders and driver datasets, carry out the full analytical plan: run the SQL query, import the driver roster, clean and model the data, compute zone-level statistics, and build the summary visualization. Record any decisions or changes you make in a decision log.

public.instruction: Complete the QuickShip capstone project's execution independently against its plan, across the SQL, spreadsheet, and Python/pandas tools it requires. Maintain a decision log throughout. Submit your completed capstone artefact (queries, cleaned data, model, statistics, and figures) together with a short decision log.
checklist: Completed SQL query retrieving the orders table.
Completed read_excel() import of the driver roster.
Cleaned data with missing values handled.
Joined orders and drivers tables using driver_id.
Decision log records changes made to the original plan, how data-quality issues were handled, and a check that outputs still answer the original question.

rubric.criterion: Submits a completed capstone artefact (queries, cleaned data, model, statistics, and figures).
Decision log records changes made to the original plan.
Decision log records how data-quality issues were handled.
Decision log includes a check that outputs still answer the original analytical question.

correct.message: Well done. You completed the capstone independently and maintained a decision log that records changes, data-quality decisions, and a check that the outputs still answer the original question.

incorrect.message: Make sure your submission includes both the completed artefact and a decision log. The log must record changes to the plan, how data-quality issues were handled, and a check that the outputs still answer the original question.

hints: The decision log is not optional — it is what makes the analysis transparent and evaluable.
Check that your outputs answer the original scoped question: which zones miss the 25-minute target, and by how much?

steps.title: Turning Findings into a Story for the Operations Team
steps.lede: The finished analysis now needs to be turned into something the operations team can act on: a narrated stakeholder summary of what was found.

blocks.text: Designing a communication with a specific person in mind — even if that is not always the reality — can help avoid treating a 'mixed audience' as one undifferentiated group. Knowing what motivates that audience lets you frame what you need them to know or do in those terms. So instead of writing for 'the operations team', write for the Head of Operations specifically.

before.title: Raw analytical finding

nodes.label:
Lagos-North: avg 32.9 min, 0% on time, gap 7.9 min above target
Lagos-South: avg 29.0 min, 0% on time, gap 4.0 min above target
Kano-Central: avg 26.0 min, 33.3% on time, gap 1.0 min above target
Abuja-West: avg 22.6 min, 100% on time

before.alt_text: Table of zone-level delivery statistics: Lagos-North and Lagos-South both miss the 25-minute target; Kano-Central barely misses; Abuja-West is fully on target.

after.title: Narrated stakeholder summary

nodes.label:
Beginning: Last quarter, QuickShip's delivery-time target is 25 minutes across all zones.
Middle: Lagos-North and Lagos-South are both missing the target — Lagos-North by an average of 7.9 minutes, with no orders on time.
End: Adding one courier to the Lagos route is the recommended next step.

after.alt_text: Narrated summary paragraph structured as beginning (context), middle (finding), end (recommendation) for the Head of Operations.

blocks.change_summary: The same zone-delay data is transformed into an audience-facing story: context first, then the key finding, then a recommended action — framed for the Head of Operations.

steps.title: Beginning, Middle, End — and What Counts as Sufficient
steps.lede: A summary can follow a story structure with an obvious beginning, middle, and end.

blocks.text: The beginning level-sets the audience with the big picture and background context. The middle presents what the analysis found. The ending gives the key takeaway — such as a recommended next step. For the QuickShip capstone, the beginning sets the delivery-time target, the middle reports the Lagos slowdown, and the ending recommends adding one courier to the Lagos route.

During delivery, insights are communicated to the people who need them, sufficiently for them to determine whether the work meets their requirements. This communication can include summary packs, reports, or presentations. For the capstone, the finished summary pack should let the Head of Operations judge whether the analysis answers the original question.
A narrated summary aimed at one specific person, moving through beginning, middle, and end, is what turns the capstone's findings into something its audience can actually use.

steps.title: What Counts as Sufficient Delivery?
steps.lede: The Head of Operations receives the capstone summary pack. What is the standard for whether the delivery is sufficient?

public.prompt: The Head of Operations receives the QuickShip capstone summary pack. What is the standard for whether the delivery is sufficient?

options.text: The summary pack lets the Head of Operations determine whether the work meets their requirements — whether it answers the original question.
The summary pack is at least five pages long and includes all the raw data.
The summary pack includes all the technical details of the SQL queries and Python code used.
The summary pack has been approved by the data team before being sent to the operations team.

opt_sufficient.message: Correct. During delivery, insights are communicated to the people who need them, sufficiently for them to determine whether the work meets their requirements. The standard is whether the Head of Operations can judge whether the analysis answers the original question.

opt_length.message: Length and inclusion of raw data are not the standard for sufficiency. The standard is whether the recipient can determine whether the work meets their requirements — whether it answers the original question.

opt_technical.message: Technical details of the implementation are not the standard for sufficiency. The standard is whether the Head of Operations can determine whether the analysis answers the original question — not whether they can reproduce the SQL queries.

opt_approval.message: Internal approval is not the standard for sufficiency. The standard is whether the recipient — the Head of Operations — can determine whether the work meets their requirements.

correct.message: Right. Delivery is sufficient when the recipient can determine whether the work meets their requirements. For the capstone, that means the Head of Operations can judge whether the analysis answers the original question.

incorrect.message: The standard for sufficiency is not length, technical detail, or internal approval. It is whether the recipient can determine whether the work meets their requirements.

hints: Who is the audience for the delivery, and what do they need to be able to do with it?
Sufficiency is about the recipient's ability to evaluate the work — not about the format or length.

steps.title: Write the Narrated Stakeholder Summary
steps.lede: Using the QuickShip zone delivery summary, write a narrated stakeholder summary for the Head of Operations. Structure it with a clear beginning (context), middle (findings), and end (recommendation). Submit your summary pack.

public.instruction: Using the QuickShip zone delivery summary, write a narrated stakeholder summary addressed to the Head of Operations. Structure it with a clear beginning (business context and the 25-minute delivery target), middle (the zone-delay finding with key numbers), and end (a recommended next step). Frame the finding in terms that motivate the Head of Operations. Submit your summary pack.
checklist: Beginning: states the business context and the 25-minute delivery target.
Middle: names the specific zones missing the target and by how much (e.g. Lagos-North: avg 32.9 min, gap 7.9 min).
End: gives a recommended next step.
Addressed to the Head of Operations — framed around what they care about.
No unexplained technical detail (no SQL, no Python code).

rubric.criterion: Has a clear beginning that states the business context and the 25-minute delivery target.
Middle presents the specific zone-delay finding with numbers (zones and gap in minutes).
End gives a recommended next step.
Addressed to a named audience role and framed in terms that audience cares about.
Does not include unexplained technical detail.

correct.message: Well done. Your summary has a clear beginning (context and target), middle (specific zone findings with numbers), and end (recommended next step), framed for the Head of Operations.

incorrect.message: Check your summary against the checklist: does it have a beginning (context and target), a middle (specific zones and gap numbers), and an end (recommended next step)? Is it framed for the Head of Operations without unexplained technical detail?

hints: The beginning should answer: what is this report about, and why does it matter to the Head of Operations?
The middle should name specific zones and their gap above the 25-minute target — use the numbers from the zone summary.

steps.title: Packaging the Work So Others Can Evaluate It
steps.lede: The very last capstone step: package the finished work so someone who never watched it get built can understand and evaluate it.

blocks.text: Transparency about the analytical decisions, process, limitations, and changes made at each stage should be clearly shown through documentation of the analysis, assumptions, and data, together with records of the decisions and quality-assurance checks made. For the capstone, that means documenting the decisions made at each stage — from scoping through visualization.

Delivery and communication activities can include producing summary packs and reports, launching dashboards or websites, and giving presentations. The capstone's deliverable is the finished report or summary pack, together with the visualization set already built, presented to the operations team that raised the original complaint.

blocks.title: Documentation layer → Delivery layer

nodes.label: Delivery layer
nodes.detail: Summary pack + visualizations + presentation to operations team

blocks.alt_text: Two-layer structure: a documentation layer capturing decisions and QA checks at each prior stage (Scope → Retrieve → Clean → Model → Analyze → Visualize), feeding into a delivery layer comprising the summary pack, visualizations, and presentation to the operations team.

steps.title: Delivery Formats
steps.lede: Which of the following is NOT listed as a delivery and communication activity for the capstone?

public.prompt: Which of the following is a valid delivery and communication activity for the QuickShip capstone?

options.text: Producing a summary pack and presenting it to the operations team that raised the original complaint.
Sending the raw orders table and driver roster to the operations team for them to analyze themselves.
Sharing the Python notebook with the SQL queries and pandas code, without any narrative.
Filing the analysis in an internal data team repository without communicating it to the operations team.

opt_summary_pack.message: Correct. Delivery and communication activities can include producing summary packs and reports, launching dashboards or websites, and giving presentations. The capstone's deliverable is the finished report or summary pack, presented to the operations team that raised the original complaint.

opt_raw_data.message: Sending raw data is not a delivery activity — it transfers the analytical work to the stakeholder rather than communicating insights. Delivery means communicating the insights to the people who need them.

opt_code_only.message: Sharing code without a narrative does not communicate insights to a non-technical audience. Delivery activities include summary packs, reports, and presentations — not raw code.

opt_internal_only.message: Filing the analysis internally without communicating it to the operations team means the insights never reach the people who need them. Delivery means communicating to the commissioner and approver.

correct.message: Right. Delivery activities include summary packs, reports, dashboards, and presentations — communicated to the people who need the insights.

incorrect.message: Delivery means communicating insights to the people who need them. Valid formats include summary packs, reports, dashboards, and presentations — not raw data, code, or internal filing.

hints: Who is the audience for the capstone delivery?
Delivery activities communicate insights — they do not transfer raw data or code.

steps.title: Assemble the Capstone Deliverable
steps.lede: Compile your QuickShip capstone work into a complete deliverable: a documentation section covering decisions and QA checks at each stage, plus the summary pack, visualizations, and a short presentation for the operations team.

public.instruction: Write up and present the finished QuickShip capstone project as a polished deliverable. Produce a documentation section that records the key analytical decisions, assumptions, data-handling choices, and quality-assurance checks made at each stage. Then assemble the finished report or summary pack together with the visualization set and present it to the operations team.
checklist: Documentation section records at least three analytical decisions or assumptions (e.g. how missing values were handled, how the time period was defined, how the join key was verified).
Documentation covers decisions at multiple stages (e.g. scoping, cleaning, modeling).
Completed summary pack or report paired with the visualization set.
Plain-language narrative addressed to the stakeholder who raised the original question.
No unexplained technical jargon in the stakeholder-facing narrative.

rubric.criterion: Documentation section explicitly records at least three analytical decisions or assumptions.
Documentation covers decisions at multiple stages of the workflow.
Completed summary pack or report paired with the visualization set.
Plain-language narrative addressed to the stakeholder who raised the original question.

correct.message: Well done. Your deliverable includes a documentation section with explicit analytical decisions and a completed summary pack with visualizations, addressed to the operations team.

incorrect.message: Check your submission against the checklist: does the documentation section record at least three analytical decisions? Does the summary pack include visualizations and a plain-language narrative for the operations team?

hints: The documentation section should record decisions at each stage — scoping, cleaning, modeling, analysis.
The summary pack is for the operations team — it should be in plain language, not technical jargon.

steps.title: What You Learned
steps.lede: Three ideas that complete the capstone.

blocks.text: Independent execution is running the whole plan yourself, adjusting it as needed, and keeping a decision log along the way. A narrated summary aimed at one specific person — moving through beginning, middle, and end — turns findings into something the audience can act on. Documenting the decisions made and presenting the finished report and visuals together is what makes the capstone a deliverable someone else can evaluate.

remediation_steps.title: Design Phase vs. Analysis Phase
remediation_steps.lede: Independent execution has two distinct phases — and both produce something.

blocks.text: During the design phase, the commission is converted into an analytical plan, with some iteration expected. During the analysis phase, the planned analysis is carried out while progress and relevance are monitored, and records of the analysis conducted, changes, decisions, and assumptions made are maintained. The design phase produces the plan; the analysis phase produces the outputs and the decision log.

remediation_steps.title: Beginning, Middle, End — Applied
remediation_steps.lede: A story structure makes the summary usable, not just readable.

blocks.text: The beginning level-sets the audience with the big picture and background context. The middle presents what the analysis found. The ending gives the key takeaway, such as a recommended next step. For the QuickShip capstone: beginning — the 25-minute delivery target; middle — Lagos-North and Lagos-South are both missing it; end — add one courier to the Lagos route.

remediation_steps.title: Documentation Makes the Work Evaluable
remediation_steps.lede: A deliverable is not just finished work — it is finished work that someone else can understand and evaluate.

blocks.text: Transparency about the analytical decisions, process, limitations, and changes made at each stage should be clearly shown through documentation of the analysis, assumptions, and data, together with records of the decisions and quality-assurance checks made. Delivery activities can include summary packs, reports, dashboards, and presentations. Together, the documentation and the delivery layer make the capstone a deliverable someone else can evaluate — not just finished work only you understand.
